source.title: Experience League: Forms Submission Service for Edge Delivery Services

connection_how: With Edge Delivery Services for AEM Forms, your forms are authored in the Universal Editor (or in Google Sheets or Excel for simple forms), rendered on your Edge Delivery pages by the Adaptive Forms Block, and submitted to Adobe's Forms Submission Service or to AEM Publish.
product_facts: There are two documented routes. The simpler one: forms built in Marketo Engage are embedded on the site's pages with Marketo's own embed code, so each submission is a Marketo form fill. We would place the embed in a reusable page component, agree the fields, consent wording and validation with you, and collect only the data you approve. Marketo's form prefill does not work with the embed code.

The fuller one: AEM Forms adaptive forms with the Submit to Marketo Engage action, which add a rule editor, prefill and a PDF record of each submission, and can connect to Adobe Sign for e-signatures. We would use embedded Marketo forms for standard lead capture and adaptive forms where a form needs that logic.

Edge Delivery Services is Adobe's content delivery framework, a core part of Adobe Experience Manager, built for speed, simplicity and scalability. It works with your own CDN or the included Adobe-managed CDN.
Edge Delivery Services delivers the site's pages, built for speed.
We would build the site on Edge Delivery Services with its code managed and deployed directly from a GitHub repository. New content is added instantly, without a rebuild process.

Every project on Edge Delivery Services should produce a Lighthouse score of 100 for mobile and desktop, measured with Google PageSpeed Insights. Adobe's guidance is that the score is not hard to keep at 100 with continuous testing, so we would test each change.

product_facts: AEM Sites as a Cloud Service is built on Adobe's Core Components and page templates, with code deployed through Cloud Manager and pages edited visually in the Universal Editor.
AEM Sites is where the site is built, on Adobe's Core Components and page templates, and where your authors edit its pages.
We would implement AEM Sites as a Cloud Service. Code is deployed through Cloud Manager, Adobe's one route for it, so every release passes the same code quality checks.
We would start with discovery: a review of your current site's content, templates and integrations, a named team with agreed roles, and the measures of success.

How your existing content moves depends on where it sits today. From an existing AEM instance, Adobe's Content Transfer Tool moves it across. From another CMS, we would export the content, map it to the new templates and load it into AEM, agreeing the mapping and tooling with you in discovery.

For go-live we would plan a content freeze for the final content top-up, check the migrated content with you, test in the stage environment, which has the same sizing as production, and run user acceptance testing on a test subdomain before the DNS cutover, with redirects for retired URLs and rollback criteria agreed beforehand.

source.title: Experience League: Create and manage knowledge sources for Brand Concierge

connection_how: Brand Concierge has a native AEM Sites knowledge source: for AEM Sites as a Cloud Service with Content AI enabled, the concierge answers from an existing Content AI index, and Content AI Search is among the integrations Adobe recommends for the Site Advisory skill.
product_facts: Brand Concierge is Adobe's platform for conversational experiences on your website, mobile apps and other digital properties. Every conversation is grounded in your own content and guardrails.
Brand Concierge answers visitors' questions from the content you approve.

Brand Concierge answers only from the knowledge sources you configure (website pages, PDFs and product spreadsheets), not from general world knowledge. Website sources refresh on a schedule you set, so answers keep up with the pages you publish.

When a question falls outside those sources, the concierge is designed to say it does not have the information rather than generate an unsupported answer, and guardrails can exclude topics such as legal or compliance matters.

Brand Concierge is focused on anonymous visitors: it answers from the conversation and your knowledge sources, not from an individual customer's records. Questions about a customer's own account would go to your secure channels.

Before launch, it is tested against a golden set of real customer questions paired with ideal answers, including questions it should not answer; after launch, conversation transcripts are reviewed on a recurring basis.

product_facts: Brand Visibility measures how your brand appears in AI-generated answers, recommends content changes and tracks how that performance changes over time.
Brand Visibility measures how your brand appears in AI-generated answers.

Brand Visibility runs the prompts you choose on a recurring basis across the AI platforms it supports and records how your brand appears in each answer and how that changes over time. It measures the prompts you monitor: the questions people put to AI assistants themselves are not disclosed by the platforms.
Adobe's Brand Presence page lists ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and Perplexity as supported.

Its AI Visibility view opens the full AI answer behind a prompt: the response text, whether your brand was mentioned, which other brands were mentioned, whether your site was cited and the source URLs behind the answer.

The dashboards report the percentage of prompts where your brand is mentioned, how often your website is used as a source, share of voice and sentiment, and compare you with the other brands you choose to track in each market.
